candidates.title: Cauchy: A Cost-Efficient LLM Serving System through Adaptive Heterogeneous Deployment
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have intensified the need for serving LLMs that are cost-efficient and QoS-guaranteed. Existing frameworks often co-locate computationally distinct prefill and decode instances on homogeneous GPUs, overlooking their unique resource demands and under-utilizing heterogeneous GPUs. This leads to suboptimal resource utilization and increased capital expenditure. We present Cauchy, a LLM serving framework that adaptively deploys prefill and decode computation to the most suitable heterogeneous GPUs and dynamically schedules user requests. At the core of Cauchy is choosing proper GPU Combo, a conceptual GPU combination encompassing diverse GPU configurations, for their cost efficiency in running prefill-decode pairs. Cauchy deploys a set of combos to satisfy QoS requirements (e.g., goodput) of LLM inference. Cauchy further employs hierarchical scheduling to handle user requests, using opportunistic scheduling within the allocated GPU Combos and a goodput-weighted round-robin policy across GPU Combos. Dynamic autoscaling is used to stabilize the cost-efficiency in the face of surging requests. Experiments show that Cauchy achieves up to a 38.3% improvement in Tokens/USD efficiency over the state-of-the-art baselines, while maintaining strict Service Level Objectives (SLOs). Our work highlights the importance of leveraging workload and GPU heterogeneity to achieve superior cost-efficient LLM serving.
candidates.reason: prefillとdecodeを異種GPUへ適応配置し、階層スケジューリングとautoscalingでSLOを維持しながら費用効率を高めるLLMサービング研究。
candidates.library_body_check: 本文では異種GPU構成をGPU Comboとしてモデル化し、prefill/decode pairの費用効率に基づく配置、Combo内opportunistic scheduling、Combo間goodput-weighted round robin、需要急増時のautoscalingを組み合わせる。SLOを維持しTokens/USDを既存方式比最大38.3%改善する。

candidates.title: MX+: Pushing the Limits of Microscaling Formats for Efficient Large Language Model Serving
candidates.abstract: Reduced-precision data formats are crucial for cost-effective serving of large language models (LLMs). While numerous reduced-precision formats have been introduced thus far, they often require intrusive modifications to the software frameworks or are rather unconventional for widespread adoption across hardware vendors. In this paper, we instead focus on recent industry-driven variants of block floating-point (BFP) formats and conduct a comprehensive analysis to push their limits for efficient LLM serving. Our analysis shows that existing ultra low-bit BFP variants struggle to provide reasonable language model performance due to outlier values in blocks. To address the outliers with BFPs, we propose MX+, a cost-effective and non-intrusive extension designed for seamless integration into the microscaling (MX) formats. MX+ builds on the key insight that the outlier does not need to use its exponent field in the element data type, which allows us to repurpose the exponent field as an extended mantissa to increase the precision of the outlier element. Our evaluation shows that MX+ achieves significantly higher model performance compared to the 4-bit MX format (MXFP4) with negligible storage overhead and slowdown, thus offering a compelling alternative to MXFP4 or MXFP6 for efficient LLM inference.
candidates.reason: LLMサービング向け4bitマイクロスケーリング形式の外れ値表現を改善し、低bit推論の品質と実行効率を両立する量子化・ハードウェア協調研究。
candidates.library_body_check: 本文ではblock maximum要素の指数部が冗長になる点を利用し、そのbitを拡張mantissaへ再利用してoutlier精度を高めるMX+を提案。MXFP4より高いモデル品質を僅かなstorage/速度overheadで実現し、LLM prefill/decode向けhardware-aware実装を評価する。
